Hull studies bounded finite-population ATEs, establishes independent random assignment as optimal, and extends from affine to arbitrary estimators; the source is a two-arm ATE result.
Bai's minimax formulation assumes an H-invariant superpopulation class and optimizes linear estimators; the complete-invariance specialization yields a difference-in-means/Neyman-allocation result.
The paper studies multi-arm sequential adaptivity with Stein-like shrinkage, Gaussian-quadratic-form risk calculations, and a sequential allocation algorithm.
